Hi Dana / Tom —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday and for moving forward with Redwood. The deal team and finance wanted to outline three common approaches we see for multi-year prepays and get your preference so we can finalize the SOW and billing instructions. High level options: 

1) Split invoices by fiscal year (recommended for customer accounting): Redwood issues an invoice for Year 1 at execution and a second invoice for Year 2 at the start of that fiscal year. Each invoice is for the prorated amount for that year and recognized by Redwood over the corresponding service period.

2) Single upfront prepay with internal allocation: Customer pays the full committed amount upfront; Redwood issues one payment request but records cash to deferred revenue and recognizes revenue monthly over the two-year service period. We can provide a revrec schedule for your GL.

3) Hybrid: Invoice upfront for an initial ramp/implementation tranche and schedule the remaining year(s) as future invoices tied to PO acceptance (helps customer cashflow while keeping year boundaries tidy).

A few notes: discounts in the SOW are applied to the total committed value; we can allocate the discount pro rata across invoices or front-load it to the first invoice if you prefer (this may affect your internal expense accounting). Please confirm: (a) preferred invoicing option, (b) correct billing contact and PO number to reference, and (c) whether you need separate invoices per Redwood legal entity for tax reasons.

Attached: Signed_SOW_v1.pdf (stub).

If it helps, I can loop in our finance lead Marissa to confirm the revrec mechanics we’ll present in the contract.

Hi all —

Thanks, Hannah. Quick guidance from finance on the options: 

• If Acme wants separate fiscal-period accounting, the cleanest approach is to issue distinct invoices aligned to their fiscal years. Invoice #1 on execution for Year 1, Invoice #2 on or right before their FY start for Year 2. Redwood will recognize revenue over the service period tied to each invoice (i.e., revenue for Year 1 recognized across that year).

• If Acme needs to pay the full amount now but wants the accounting benefit of multi-year recognition, we can accept full prepayment and post the cash to deferred revenue on Redwood's books. We would then release revenue monthly over the two-year contract. We'll provide a revrec schedule CSV for their GL team to reconcile (attached).

• Discount handling: standard practice is to apply the negotiated discount to the total committed value and then allocate the discounted amounts pro rata across invoice lines for revenue recognition. If procurement requires the discount to be reflected on a specific invoice (e.g., front-loaded), we can do that, but it will alter the invoice-level amounts and we should document the allocation method in the SOW/Invoice memo for audit.

• PO / tax: Using the same PO number across invoices is fine; please confirm PO line items and tax jurisdiction (state). If multiple Redwood legal entities are involved we need to match entity on the invoice for VAT/sales tax.

Next steps for us: 
1) Confirm approach (split invoices vs single prepay).
2) Provide exact PO number(s) and billing contact.
3) We will produce draft invoices and the revrec schedule for Acme to share with their ER/GL team.

Attached: revrec_schedule.csv (stub) — sample monthly recognition schedule for the proposed allocation.

Happy to jump on a 15-min call if Acme wants to walk through the schedule.

Thanks,
